chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who fasts a fast that he has stipulated upon himself, or who fasts from the Sacred Months, and the month and the two months pass by him without him fulfilling it. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He should not fast during the journey, nor should he make up anything from the voluntary fasts except the three days which he used to fast from each month, and he should not make them equal in status to the obligatory [fasts], except that I love for you that you remain constant upon the righteous deed.'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'And as for the one who fasts the Sacred Months, it suffices him that he fasts three days in place of each month from the Sacred Months.'

key_terms.يَقْضِيهِ: He makes it up / fulfills it

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for making up missed voluntary fasts or fasting the Sacred Months?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the distinction between *Nadhr* (vow) and *Nafl* (voluntary) fasting, establishing that missed voluntary vows do not carry the strict penalty of obligatory fasts. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes the virtue of consistency (*Dawam*) over rigid compensation, allowing a simplified makeup of three days per month even for vows tied to the Sacred Months. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle of easing burdens in voluntary acts while preserving the spirit of devotion.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who had timed it upon himself, or he was Fasting from Sacred Months. So the month, and the two month pass by him, not fulfilling it. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should not be Fasting during the journey, nor would he make up for anything from the optional Fasts except for the three days which he had Fasted from each month, nor make it to be at the status of the Obligatory, except that I<sup>asws</sup> like it for you that you should be habitual upon the righteous deed’.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And the one who had the Fasting for the Sacred Months which he used to Fast, it would suffice him in place of each month from the Sacred Months, (the Fasting of) three days’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who fasts because of what he has timed upon himself or to fast of the sacred months and then one or two months pass during which he does not fast at all. He (the Imam) said, ‘He is not required to fast on a journey and there is not anything of Qada’ (compensatory fast) for optional fast except the three days that he would fast every month. He must not take it as obligatory except that I like you to continue with a good deed.’
He (the Imam) said, ’For the one committing himself to fast in the sacred months, fasting of three days, instead of fasting the whole of sacred month, is sufficient.’”
